subject.title: [Bug]: Ctrl+C not working in Windows install on foreground

question: Should maintainers require native Windows npm-global Ctrl+C reproduction before queuing a new fix for this issue?
rationale: Current source only proves shutdown after SIGINT is delivered, while the reported failure may be Windows console or npm-shim signal delivery rather than gateway shutdown logic.

options.title: Require Windows proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open until current main or the latest package is checked in a native Windows npm-global foreground run with at least PowerShell or cmd.exe.

options.title: Queue a narrow signal bridge
options.body: If maintainers accept the reporter and closed-PR proof as sufficient, queue only the Windows keypress/signal bridge with terminal cleanup and focused tests.

recommendation.title: Require Windows proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until current main or the latest package is checked in a native Windows npm-global foreground run with at least PowerShell or cmd.exe.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the gateway CLI lifecycle and docs path points to steipete.
